questions.q: What is the key trick for islands?
options: day − row number is constant inside an island
why: Sum increases twice as fast; no use.

questions.q: Days 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11. How long is the longest island?
questions.why: Islands: {3,4,5} (3 days) and {8,9,10,11} (4 days). The longest is 4.

questions.q: Scenario: you run the one-pass method on a list with duplicates 5, 5, 6. You get a streak of 3. What went wrong?
why: Correct: the real streak is 2 days.

questions.q: Scenario: a table has many users. Which is correct?
options: Compute the key per user (partition by user)
One global row number is fine
why: A global row number mixes users.

questions.q: What is the time cost of the one-pass method after sorting?
why: The sort is the n log n part only.

questions.q: Scenario: you need streaks of consecutive HOURS with an alert on. What changes?
options: Use the hour number (or divide the time difference by 1 hour)
why: Correct: the 'consecutive' step is now one hour.
Days would merge or split wrongly.
You still need a one-hour step.
